name: Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim al-Laythī
summary: Basran reader of the Qurʾān and student of Abū al-Aswad, remembered as one of the first to put dots on the letters of the Qurʾān to tell them apart.
bio: Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim was a reader of the Qurʾān in Basra and one of the students of Abū al-Aswad al-Duʾalī; al-Zubaydī puts him first in the second generation of Basran grammarians, beside Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmur, ʿAnbasa al-Fīl and Maymūn al-Aqran. He died in 89/708.

The tradition credits him, with Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmur, with the dots that distinguish letters of the same shape (bāʾ, tāʾ, thāʾ), added to copies of the Qurʾān in the time of the governor al-Ḥajjāj, after Abū al-Aswad's dots for the vowels. In al-Zubaydī's account of Abū al-Aswad, 'a man of Banū Layth' added chapters to his first book of grammar, which some take to mean Naṣr.
uncertain: Which dots were his, and which Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmur's or later readers', the sources do not agree.
